habitat: Subtropical/tropical moist lowland forests; mangrove forests; secondary growth; and plantations
story: Few birds capture the imagination quite like the Chestnut Breasted Malkoha (Phaenicophaeus curvirostris). As a member of the Cuculidae family, it has carved out a unique niche in Subtropical/tropical moist lowland forests; mangrove forests; secondary growth; and plantations. Its conservation status is Least Concern (LC), a classification that drives crucial research and protection efforts. The Chestnut Breasted Malkoha's presence is a vital sign of its ecosystem's health, making its preservation a priority. This poster is a tribute to the Chestnut Breasted Malkoha, celebrating its role in the natural world and inspiring a deeper appreciation for biodiversity.
